summary: Iteration 26: event edit (PATCH + notify + capacity/waitlist + reminded_for reset), date/venue polls (create/vote toggle/lock), photo likes & comments, attendance check-in + staff profile events_attended, and AGTS favourite places (CRUD/like/filters/search) plus Drive button. Backend 14/14 pytest pass. Frontend all requested flows pass on a 375x667 viewport: organiser Edit event prefilled form ('Edit event' title, no Repeats, 'Save changes' updates the event and the responder is notified), date poll created through the UI (dd-mm-yyyy validation works) with vote, voter names and 'Lock in' (sets date, shows 'Poll result' with a trophy, voting disabled), photo viewer heart toggle and comment, 'Who turned up?' checklist on past events only (non-organisers see 'Who came · N'), staff profile 'Team events attended · 1', Drive 'AGTS favourite places to eat & drink' button -> /places with add/validation/duplicate toast/like/Eat-Drink filters/search/owner-only delete. No critical bugs. Only minor UX and logic notes below. No deprecated Expo packages found.

minor.issue: There is no check for poll.closed, so an organiser can lock again with a different option after the poll is closed. That silently changes the date or venue and notifies every staff member again.
Creating a poll when one already exists overwrites it without warning, and all existing votes are lost (open or closed). Consider returning 409 or requiring an explicit replace.
voter_names is pulled by name ($pull by user['name']). If two staff share the same name, one person un-voting removes both names. Derive voter names from the user_ids in votes instead.
Every like after an unlike sends the photo owner another 'X liked your photo' notification, so toggling can spam the owner. Consider de-duplicating.
The date is not checked against today, so an organiser can move a future event into the past. This may be intended so attendance can be recorded, but it is not validated.

issues: 'Lock in <option>' runs straight away with no confirmation, and it notifies the whole company. A stray tap locks the poll. Add a confirm step.
A 'Lock in' ghost button under every option makes a long list. Consider one 'Lock in winner' action or a confirm sheet.
'Poll the team / Start a date or venue poll' still shows on past events.
'Who turned up?' only lists people who RSVPed. The organiser (if they did not RSVP) and walk-ins cannot be ticked.
The delete (trash) button removes a place immediately with no confirmation, including places other people have liked.
In the add form, the 'Type' chips sit tight against the next 'Address or suburb' label (little bottom spacing).

The 'AGTS favourite places to eat & drink' button uses the same outlined style as the Therapist/Participants folder tabs, so it reads like a third tab rather than a link to another screen. Consider a distinct style or a chevron icon.

action_items: (Minor) lock_poll: reject with 400 if poll.closed is already true, or confirm a re-lock.
(Minor) create_poll: return 409 if a poll exists, or warn in the UI before replacing it.
(Minor) vote: build voters from user_ids rather than pulling voter_names by name.
(UX) Add confirmation before 'Lock in' on polls and before deleting a place.
(UX) Hide 'Start a date or venue poll' on past events. Optionally let the organiser add themselves or non-RSVP staff to the attendance list.
critical_code_review_comments: events.py is 585 lines, close to the 700-line limit. Consider moving polls, photo social and attendance into routes/event_social.py.
lock_poll and create_poll use all_user_ids() to notify every user, including hidden or test users. This is consistent with create_event.
like_photo returns like_count from a stale read, which is fine for a single user. places like returns only {liked} and the client refetches, which is OK.
